recommended_title: Recalibrating the Control Variate in Prediction-Powered Mean Intervals: Small, Regime-Dependent Width Gains over PPI++ with Fixed Labels, Unlabeled Data, and Predictor
central_question: When the labeled set, unlabeled set and predictor are all fixed, can a cross-fitted recalibration of the predictor output (added as a second control variate to PPI++) shorten a valid confidence interval for a population mean, by how much, and in which regimes does it help or fail?
central_thesis: Adding a cross-fitted monotone/binned recalibration g(Yhat) as an extra control variate nested around PPI++ gives a small but measurable average narrowing of mean intervals (about 2% in geometric-mean width on held-out sealed pools, ~7% vs PPI lambda=1, ~30% vs classical), concentrated where the predictor is miscalibrated (census income, plankton, miscalibrated synthetic) and near zero where the raw prediction is already well calibrated, with empirical coverage held at a level the evaluator's exact binomial tests did not reject but whose point estimates (pooled 0.934, minimum family 0.91) sit below the nominal 0.95.
narrative_rationale: The completed final evaluation is outcome=qualified (final.qualification.outcome), status=completed, correct=true, claim_status_code=2 (narrower than PPI++ with coverage not rejected, by a paired bootstrap lower bound on the aggregate score), so a conditional-support paper is grounded. The task itself welcomes conditional answers, and the strongest honest story is a bounded one: the PPI++ interval is not the shortest valid interval, but the headroom reachable with only (Y, Yhat) on the fixed inputs is small and regime dependent, which matches the efficiency-bound view (gain = drop from Var(Y - lambda*Yhat) to Var(Y - E[Y|Yhat])). Search and final are kept separate: three model variants were all scored in search (no unscored attempts), the frozen one was evaluated once on a disjoint sealed set of pools. Coverage point estimates below 0.95 and the absence of ablations/CIs on width ratios are central limitations and must be foregrounded, not hidden. No downstream_study block exists in paper_data, so none is used.
edit_framing_decision: Edit mode is not active (no previous_paper, no edit context files); a fresh framing was chosen. Candidate framings compared: (a) 'new method beats PPI++' headline - rejected because gains are ~2% and coverage is below nominal in point estimate; (b) 'label-free spline basis / stacked calibration as the contribution' - rejected because those variants scored lower or comparable in search and the stacked variant did not beat the simpler one; (c) conditional/limits paper centred on recalibrated control variates plus an efficiency-bound analysis of when gain is possible - selected.
staged_input_impact: No staged prior manuscript, new-program or old-program inputs are present; framing derives only from paper_data.json final_evaluation, the three scored search attempts, the task contract/evaluators and the frozen program source.

method_groups.name: Classical labeled-only interval and PPI (lambda=1)
method_groups.include_reason: Reference points that the evaluator reports directly (final mean log width ratio 0.358 vs classical and 0.070 vs PPI lambda=1, positive = narrower); show how much of the total gain over labeled-only inference is already captured by existing PPI machinery.

method_groups.name: PPI++ (power-tuned scalar lambda on raw Yhat)
method_groups.include_reason: The primary comparator for every width ratio and the score; also the fallback nested inside the proposed interval.

method_groups.name: Cross-fitted recalibrated PPI (isotonic and quantile-binned g(Yhat); [Yhat, g] as control variates with variance-minimising weights; Student-t critical value; adopt the recalibrated interval only if its half-width is at least 1% below PPI++)
method_groups.include_reason: The frozen search winner and the method evaluated in the sealed final; the paper's studied object.

method_groups.name: Stratified PPI (quantile bins of Yhat, lambda=1 per stratum)
method_groups.include_reason: Implemented in the frozen program as a comparison estimator and relevant prior work; include only as a method description/related work unless evaluator-reported numbers exist for it (none appear in paper_data: do not report numeric results for it).

method_groups.name: Search-stage alternative variants: label-free hinge-basis control variates with PRESS selection; repeated cross-fitted NNLS-stacked calibration
method_groups.include_reason: Two scored alternative designs give a design-space contrast (search combined scores 0.0046 and 0.0223 vs 0.0271 for the winner). Present as a single-evaluation design comparison on search pools, not as controlled ablations, and without uncertainty claims.

results_focus: Sealed final evaluation (5 families, each 100 independent labeled/unlabeled draws, n=500, N=20000 for the four real pools; synthetic mixes four regimes, n in {200,500}, N in {2000,20000}): per-family log width ratio vs PPI++ (census_income 0.0287, census_healthcare 0.0018, census_education 0.0023, plankton 0.0359, synthetic 0.0413), aggregate 0.0220; convert to width reductions (1-exp(-s)) as derived values and say so.

Aggregate narrowing vs the three comparators: 0.022 (PPI++), 0.070 (PPI lambda=1), 0.358 (classical) mean log ratios; make clear that most of the gain over labeled-only inference comes from PPI itself and recalibration adds a small increment.

Validity reporting: pooled coverage 0.934 and minimum-family coverage 0.91 vs nominal 0.95; evaluator gate (exact one-sided binomial tests, pooled level 0.01, per-family Bonferroni) not rejected, controls (constant predictor, permuted predictor, shift) passed, 0 failed episodes. State that the point estimates are below nominal and the gate is a non-rejection, not proof of nominal coverage; per-family coverage other than the minimum is not available.

Where gain exists vs not: gains largest on synthetic (nonlinear miscalibrated regime is the designed case), plankton and census_income; near zero on census_healthcare and census_education. Do not attribute causes beyond what the analytic argument and predictor-calibration reasoning support; no per-regime ablation was run, so mechanisms are hypotheses unless a derivation backs them.

Stability across five evaluator partitions of the final run (partition scores 0.0203, 0.0213, 0.0220, 0.0235, 0.0247; derived range only; these are reset-seed partitions of one evaluator protocol, not independent method trainings, and candidate diagnostics trust is 'unverified'); report as spread, not as a confidence interval.

Search-stage design contrast on disjoint search pools (galaxies, forest, gene_expression, alphafold, synthetic; scored attempts 3 of 3, none unscored): winner 0.0271, stacked-calibration 0.0223, label-free basis 0.0046; per-family log ratios vs PPI++ for the winner: alphafold 0.0104, forest 0.0168, galaxies 0.0035, gene_expression 0.0290, synthetic 0.0757. Search coverage pooled 0.943 / min family 0.933 for the winner; the stacked variant had min family 0.917. Label the contrast as single evaluations; separate it clearly from final results.

Analytic section: asymptotic variance with control variates [Yhat, g]; PPI++ is nested (lambda on Yhat only), recalibrated gain governed by reduction from Var(Y - lambda*Yhat) to residual variance of the best g, bounded below by Var(Y - E[Y|Yhat]) when only Yhat is used; list assumptions (iid labeled/unlabeled from one population, fixed predictor, mean estimand, alpha=0.05, finite second moments, cross-fitted g at adequate rate) and no-gain conditions (already-linear calibration, uninformative predictor, small n). State explicitly that a numeric theory-vs-observed width-ratio check is not part of the available artifacts and was not performed.

planned_subsections.heading: Estimator specification and hyperparameters
planned_subsections.grounded_content: Exact form of the frozen interval: PPI++ closed-form lambda clipped to [0,1]; 5-fold cross-fitted isotonic (direction by correlation sign) and quantile-binned g (bins = min(10, max(2, floor(0.8n/25)))); [Yhat, g] standardised control variates with ridge-stabilised variance-minimising weights; Student-t critical value with df = n-1-p via Cornish-Fisher; 1% half-width margin rule vs PPI++; classical fallback on non-finite output. Taken from the frozen program source.

notes_for_writer: Qualification facts come from final.qualification.*: outcome=qualified, status=completed, correct=true. Do not say the method failed qualification; also do not turn 'qualified' into a generalization or superiority claim. It means the evaluator found valid-by-gate coverage and an aggregate width gain over PPI++ whose paired-bootstrap lower bound was positive (claim_status_code=2); the bootstrap value itself is not in paper_data.

Be candid that pooled coverage 0.934 and min-family 0.91 are below 0.95; the gate is non-rejection with 500 pooled and 100 per-family draws. Do not claim nominal coverage was attained. Avoid inferring cause (Wald/t approximation, selection among candidates) unless supported by a derivation, and label it a hypothesis.

Search scores (single evaluation each, disjoint pools, smaller n/N such as forest n=100, N=1000) and final scores are different evaluations; never pool them or rank variants by search score differences as if statistically established. Winner-vs-stacked difference (0.0271 vs 0.0223) is small and has no uncertainty estimate.
Width differences are ratios of summed widths over a family's draws (not per-draw paired CIs); say so. Derived percentages (1-exp(-s)) are computations on reported values; present them as derived.

No ablation artifacts exist (evidence_sources.ablations is missing). Describe the isotonic/binned/fallback components, but do not claim component-level attributions; state which questions remain open (effect of K, bins, margin, t vs normal, n sweep, small-n regime).

The task also asked about other estimands and a labeled-size sweep; the artifacts cover only the mean estimand, alpha=0.05, with n=500 on real pools. Scope statements must reflect that; ballots and other pools were not part of final scoring and no real-data n sweep was scored.
